questions.q: Why is a drone's configuration code?
options: Whether it flies depends on it
questions.explain: Whether the aircraft flies depends on its configuration, so it needs history, review, checks and rollback.

questions.q: What should a commit message for a parameter change contain?
options: The change date and the author's name

questions.q: How do you check that a SITL failsafe test really works?
options: Run it twice in a row
Break the config and watch it fail
questions.explain: A test that cannot fail proves nothing.

questions.q: Why normalize the diff all before committing?
options: So the diff shows what matters
So that Git LFS can store it as text

questions.q: Where should large binary logs be kept?
What is a release tag in the context of a drone?
options: A label on the config you flew with
The flight number in the operator's log
questions.explain: git checkout <tag> -- <folder> brings the config back.

options: A rule checked against every config
A parameter that cannot be read
A backup of the configuration on an external flash drive
questions.explain: For example, "failsafe is enabled": a CI check on every change.

questions.q: Why have a second person review parameter changes?
options: To catch a mistake before the flight, not after
questions.explain: A fresh pair of eyes catches typos and misunderstood consequences before takeoff.
